facts.heading: Anxiety worsened since September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this feeling has worsened since September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time, and it's got worse since September.

facts.heading: Made deputy head at school
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school in September.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school.

facts.heading: Taught Year 4 for eleven years
facts.content: Hannah has taught Year 4 for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Worries about competence in role
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she does not know what she is doing in her new role.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety peaks Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxiety is mostly felt on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings.

facts.heading: Rehearses meetings in head
facts.content: When anxiety hits, Hannah rehearses Monday's staff meeting in her head.
facts.evidence: My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Last week, Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Worried about Mr Hargreaves' opinion
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding a policy change.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.heading: Feels like lying to Mr Hargreaves
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr Hargreaves about being capable.
facts.evidence: I feel I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Feels like wearing mother's coat
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a headteacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for twenty years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for twenty years.

facts.heading: Compares self to mother's career
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to what she thinks her mother would have done.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother is supportive but dismissive
facts.content: Hannah's mother says she worries too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Hides feelings from mother
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad things are because it makes her feel like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: So I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Wakes up at 4 AM daily
facts.content: Hannah wakes up at four every morning.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning

facts.heading: Wakes up at 4 AM with to-do list
facts.content: Hannah wakes up at four and goes through her to-do list.
facts.evidence: I fall asleep fine, then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list

facts.heading: Stressors on to-do list
facts.content: Hannah's to-do list includes timetable changes, Ofsted prep, a parent complaint, and a worried child.
facts.evidence: Timetable changes, the Ofsted prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about

facts.heading: Waking up since second week of term
facts.content: Hannah has been waking like this since about the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term

facts.heading: Drinks five or six cups of coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences her heart going fast and her hands being shaky in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky

facts.heading: Left meeting due to symptoms

facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice

facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it

facts.heading: Feels guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when her partner says she should enjoy it.
facts.evidence: Guilty, and a bit alone

facts.heading: Lost school friends after promotion

facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward

facts.heading: Misses children and class
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and her class.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too

facts.heading: Misses daily moments with children

facts.evidence: The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time

facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried

facts.heading: Last relaxed during summer holidays

facts.evidence: The summer holidays. We went walking in the Lakes

facts.heading: No expectations during holidays
facts.content: During the holidays, nobody expected anything of Hannah.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me

facts.heading: Wreck the week before term

facts.evidence: The week before term I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday

facts.evidence: It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped

facts.evidence: I stopped, because I felt silly.

facts.evidence: I'd like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
